ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: This protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of the University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) (Protocol no. 853607) and Trinity Health IRB relied on the IRB at UPenn.
All participants gave written informed consent prior to participation in this study (Institutional Review Board number: 853607).
PACE participants are generally dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid.
Participants All participants were at least 55 years old with a documented diagnosis of stroke that occurred at least 3 months prior to study enrollment.
Participants were required to have completed either a CT or MRI scan after stroke onset.
Written informed consent was obtained from all participants prior to study participation.
Clinical Assessment After being recruited, participants were consented and assessed using standard clinical and robot-based assessments.
Participants completed several motor and cognitive assessments, including the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FM-UE) upper extremity 50 and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) 51 .
table.formatted: Participants completed several motor and cognitive assessments, including the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FM-UE) upper extremity <ref type="bibr" target="#b53">50</ref> and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) <ref type="bibr" target="#b54">51</ref> .

table.text: At the end of each game, participants were asked about their enjoyment ("Did you like playing this game?") and interest ("Are you interested in playing this game again?").

At the end of the first visit, participants were also asked to rank the games according to preference, selecting the games using four superlatives ("First Favorite", "Second Favorite", "Third Favorite", "Least Favorite").
After each session, participants were asked to rate their pain on a 10-point visual analog scale (VAS) and their exertion on a 10-point Borg scale.
Four participants (006, 018, 022, and 028) had mild motor impairment and mild cognitive impairment (18 ≤ MoCA < 26).
table.formatted: Four participants (006, 018, 022, and 028) had mild motor impairment and mild cognitive impairment (18 ≤ MoCA < 26).

table.text: Mean arousal indicated that participants were initially "excited" by the system at the first survey time point (2.67 ± 1.51), but their arousal shifted to moderately simulated for the later surveys (5.0 ± 3.35, 5.0 ± 3.16).

Perceptual accessibility may have also contributed; the therapist notes indicate that participants had difficulty discriminating task-relevant colors in CoinRunner, TheraStack, and Color Switch, and all three were less frequently selected.
table.header: Selection of Games and Robot Configuration

table.text: Although initially reluctant to play the more cognitively demanding game, the therapists encouraged 029 by commenting that many other study participants were typically unable to complete those games.
Participants are routinely transported to and from the facility, where their day is planned around activities, food, and medical care.
Once participants were set up on the robotic systems, they completed their therapy with minimal supervision.
All participants gave written informed consent prior to participation in this study (Institutional Review Board number: 853607).
All participants gave written informed consent to publish their results.

At Mercy LIFE, four participants (006, 018, 022, and 024) averaged 2 therapy visit per week for 6 weeks while at Penn Medicine Rittenhouse, the two participants (028 and 029) averaged 3 therapy visits per week for 4 weeks.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

live_data_statements: PACE participants are generally dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid.
Participants All participants were at least 55 years old with a documented diagnosis of stroke that occurred at least 3 months prior to study enrollment.
Participants were required to have completed either a CT or MRI scan after stroke onset.
Written informed consent was obtained from all participants prior to study participation.
Clinical Assessment After being recruited, participants were consented and assessed using standard clinical and robot-based assessments.
Participants completed several motor and cognitive assessments, including the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FM-UE) upper extremity 50 and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) 51 .
At the end of each game, participants were asked about their enjoyment ("Did you like playing this game?") and interest ("Are you interested in playing this game again?").

At the end of the first visit, participants were also asked to rank the games according to preference, selecting the games using four superlatives ("First Favorite", "Second Favorite", "Third Favorite", "Least Favorite").
After each session, participants were asked to rate their pain on a 10-point visual analog scale (VAS) and their exertion on a 10-point Borg scale.
Four participants (006, 018, 022, and 028) had mild motor impairment and mild cognitive impairment (18 ≤ MoCA < 26).

Mean arousal indicated that participants were initially "excited" by the system at the first survey time point (2.67 ± 1.51), but their arousal shifted to moderately simulated for the later surveys (5.0 ± 3.35, 5.0 ± 3.16).

Perceptual accessibility may have also contributed; the therapist notes indicate that participants had difficulty discriminating task-relevant colors in CoinRunner, TheraStack, and Color Switch, and all three were less frequently selected.
Although initially reluctant to play the more cognitively demanding game, the therapists encouraged 029 by commenting that many other study participants were typically unable to complete those games.
Participants are routinely transported to and from the facility, where their day is planned around activities, food, and medical care.
Once participants were set up on the robotic systems, they completed their therapy with minimal supervision.
All participants gave written informed consent prior to participation in this study (Institutional Review Board number: 853607).
All participants gave written informed consent to publish their results.

At Mercy LIFE, four participants (006, 018, 022, and 024) averaged 2 therapy visit per week for 6 weeks while at Penn Medicine Rittenhouse, the two participants (028 and 029) averaged 3 therapy visits per week for 4 weeks.
